D.t: John Hickenlooper leads by 20.9 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 591,012 votes; a one point swing is about 14,159 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +12.1 and D +29.2. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Denver, a projected net 221,892 votes; Boulder, a projected net 108,651 votes; Arapahoe, a projected net 102,810 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: El Paso, R +1.0, 11.9% of the vote; Douglas, D +1.2, 7.1% of the vote; Pueblo, D +9.0, 2.7% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, John Hickenlooper runs furthest behind in Larimer, Mesa, Boulder. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 76% of voters, 54 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.77 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 73% of voters, 60 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.65 points; College graduates, 55% of voters, 61 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.75 points.
The forecast's worst groups for John Hickenlooper: Immigration voters 25 to 72, Small counties 47 to 50, Midsize counties 50 to 48. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.1M cash against $28K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Democrats cast 33% of the 824,562 ballots in Colorado so far, against 25% for the other party. That is 4.8 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.
